recipes.name: Best Green Bean Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.5 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Mix green beans and soup together in a large microwave-safe bowl until well combined. Microwave on high until warm, 3 to 5 minutes.
Stir ½ cup Cheddar into the green bean mixture. Microwave on High until heated through, 2 to 3 minutes.
Spread the mixture evenly in a 1 ½-quart casserole dish. Sprinkle with the remaining ½ cup Cheddar, then top with the French-fried onions.
Bake until the casserole is bubbling around the edges, the cheese is melted, and the onions are lightly browned, about 10 minutes. Watch closely near the end so the onions don’t burn.

raw_recipe.headline: Best Green Bean Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This best green bean casserole recipe uses only four ingredients: Canned green beans, condensed mushroom soup, French-fried onions, and Cheddar cheese.

video.description: Are you in a rush to make something for the next big holiday gathering? In this video, learn how to make a classic side dish with this easy recipe for the best green bean casserole. Combined into a dish with cream of mushroom soup, decadent cheddar cheese, and more, the green bean casserole is baked in the oven until crisp and bubbly.

review.reviewBody: This is basically our standard green bean casserole recipe with some minor modifications I've made over the years. It's ALWAYS the first to disappear at potlucks when there are other versions of green bean casseroles and people often ask why it seems to taste so much better than the original one on the French's can. I always use French-cut green beans, add a (drained) can of sliced water chestnuts (coarsely chopped) and stir 3 ounces of the French fried onions into the casserole along with ALL of the cheddar cheese. Heating the ingredients in the microwave is really an unnecessary step. Bake in a flat casserole dish 30-35 minutes or until hot in the center. Then sprinkle the other 3 ounces of French fried onions over the top and bake 5 minutes more. We much prefer the cheese stirred INTO the casserole and NOT put on top. When doubling the recipe, using one can of water chestnuts works fine since a whole can is almost too much (but we like the crunch!) for a single recipe, depending on personal taste. If I'm trying to extend the number of servings for a double recipe then I generally use 2 cans of water chestnuts for that. A tried and true yummy favorite of many – thanks, Jan!

I made some changes to this, based on what other reviewers said. I used fresh green beans, microwaved for 5-7 minutes until still crisp, and left to the side while I prepped the mixture. I used mushroom soup, cheddar cheese, and french fried onions. I also added 2-3 tablespoons of sour cream, real bacon pieces, salt, pepper, garlic/onion powders and little cayenne pepper for a slight kick. After mixture was to my liking, I folded in the green beans and baked in oven for 30-35 minutes. About 5 minutes before done, I added a layer of french fried onion on top (used all cheddar in the mixture) and heated until topping was warm. Absolutely delicious!

I liked this much more than the traditional Green Bean Casserole. The cheese is a good addition. I didn't bother with the microwave. It's not at all necessary. Just mixed it all up with 2/3 of the french fried onions. Bake for 30 mins at 350 and then top with remaining french fried onions and bake about 5 more mins to brown. 

I happened to have a LARGE (6+ lb can of green beans) that I got on a special. It's probably a perfect amount for a large Thanksgiving crowd. I drained the liquid, added 2 cans of regular cream of mushroom and 1 can of roasted garlic cream of mushroom, 2 t. salt and 1 t. pepper and 3 cups of cheddar cheese. Mixed 1- 6oz can of french fried onions into the mix and then transferred to a large casserole dish. Topped with a second can of french fried onions the last 5 mins. This would be great to make in two casserole containers and freeze one for later. I fed 10 people with it and had enough left to freeze for another meal later. I'm glad I found something everyone really liked as I have about 4 more of those LARGE cans of green beans!

It would be so nice if these recipes would indicate what size baking dish to use, instead of just "put the ingredients into a baking dish." I see more and more recipes that omit that information. For those of us who don't do a great deal of cooking or baking, it would sure be helpful.

To start off with, I made mushroom soup from scratch instead of using anything from a can. The first go, I used fresh chanterelle mushrooms and on the second go I used portobellos. The chanterelles were better, but the portobellos were good too. My soup recipe turns out fairly thick, not quite as thick as the gelatinous blob you'd get from a can, but it's "dry" enough to not make things soggy. Second, I reduced the cheese to half a cup and mixed all of it into the beans. Other than these two alterations, the recipe is the same. Here's the recipe I used for my soup. Be advised that this recipe makes 8-10 servings of soup. INGREDIENTS 4 tbsp unsalted butter 1 lg white onion, chopped 12 oz salt pork, chopped 1 & 1/2 qt chanterelle mushrooms, sliced (may sub portobellos) 1/2 cup AP flour 1 cup cold vegetable stock 1 qt light cream 1 qt water 1 lg pinch thyme 1 pinch parsley DIRECTIONS Saute onions in butter over medium heat until beginning to brown Add salt pork and cook until brown/crispy, do not drain grease Add mushrooms and saute until soft and uniformly cooked Add flour slowly while folding into mushroom mix until no raw flour is left Reduce heat to simmer Add cold vegetable stock and stir lightly Add 1/2 qt cream and thoroughly mix in until all flour is dissolved Add remainder of cream, mix Add water, mix Add herbs, mix Simmer for 20 minutes Put in refrigerator over night

I just made this for the first time, and used some of the suggestions from others. It was soooo good! Like others, I made some of the suggested modifications. I did a double recipe. I used fresh green beans and cooked them about halfway before mixing with the mushroom soup, Mexican blend cheese, and about half of the fried onions. I also added some garlic salt, about 1/2 tsp of Cayenne, about a tsp of soy sauce, and 4-5 cloves of fresh, diced garlic. I baked the whole mixture for about 20 minutes and then added more fried onions on top. I put it under the broiler but some of the onions burned quickly so I picked off the burned ones. Be careful how you do this last step to have a crispy onion top. It was still fantastic and got the most compliments of the entire meal. The flavors blend together so nicely you don't get an over-powering mushroom or cheese flavor. Even both of my picky-eater teens loved it. This one's a keeper!
Added chopped water chestnuts and bacon, and mixed all the cheese into the green bean mixture, along with half the onions. Fabulous!

Everyone loved this! I followed the recipe but rather than microwaving first, I put it in a casserole dish and baked in the oven for 30 minutes, added the remaining cheese and fried onions and baked for an additional 5 minutes. Perfect! I’ll be making this again, and not just for holidays.

Check out the sodium content! That's from the soup and the store bought fried onions. Campbell's soup is horrible for you. I make my own mushroom gravy, which is my biscuit gravy with mushrooms added. I slice my own onions on my mandolin, and batter with flour and corn starch, then fry. It's worth the extra effort.

I followed suggestion of a few others and bypassed the microwave and just poured everything into baking dish (reserving 1/4 C 
 cheese and french fried onions). I also mixed in 1/2 tsp soy sauce. Then baked 20 min. Sprinkled the french fried onions & the other 1/4 C cheese & baked 7-8 min. NOTE: THICK shredded cheese melts better.
Used Cream of Celery instead of Cream of Mushroom. Added sauteed mushrooms and onions. Cheese on top under French Onions good for keeping top crunchy.
Really a great improvement over the dated recipe!! Loved it!
I cannot believe from all the reviews not one person added Worschestsire sauce it's a must.

This recipe is hilarious. I started it without realizing it’s to microwave and busted out laughing when I got to that part. Went with it and brought it to an event and everyone raved about how great it was. Literally started calling me the green bean casserole lady. So now it’s my super secret recipe. I can’t usually boil water, my husband does all the cooking but he can’t touch my green bean casserole. It’s a basic dish but works awesome lol
I add 2 tablespoons of sour cream and I grate sharp cheddar cheese. My family loves it!
Skip the can of processed soup, the dish is soo much better if you make a cream sauce with mushroom and heavy cream and onions.
Easy delicious

For a very easy approach to a classic side dish, this recipe is a winner. I skipped microwaving stuff, not necessary. I mixed in all the cheese instead of putting it on top, and also mixed in part of the crispy onions. I baked for 30 minutes. It was an easy and delicious dish that completely disappeared!
added 1 can mushrooms drained, 2 tbls bacon bits, 1/4 pkg cream cheese. should have sauteed mushrooms and added pepper, parm cheese and used oven @350 degrees for 30 ish minutes
First time making this dish. Made it for the family for Thanksgiving, and everybody enjoyed it. Recommend topping with bacon crumbles before cooking.
